traits.note: Hutchinson (vol. 1, 2nd ed., 1959), family 110 Begoniaceae: undershrubs or herbs, mostly succulent, the stems jointed; leaves alternate, simple, often lopsided; stipules free, falling; flowers on one plant in two sexes, regular or irregular, mostly in cymes in the leaf axils, showy; the male with 2 (rarely 5) sepals and 0 to 5 petals and many stamens. The inferior ovary and the winged capsule are from common knowledge (the account is cut short in the copy read), inferred, not traced.

traits.zygomorphy.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data), family Begoniaceae: its irregular flowers are of no named kind (pea flower, two lips, orchid lip), read from the coded corolla symmetry (spec-rework/b1/delta): zygomorphy other. Its flowers are not mostly zygomorphic, so a plant of it states its own symmetry; one that is zygomorphic draws this kind, and one stating none is drawn regular.

traits.phyllotaxis_pattern.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 333, 334, 335, family Begoniaceae: phyllotaxis pattern spiral or distichous, usually; read as {"distichous": "often", "spiral": "often"}.

traits.leaf_venation.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 333, 334, 335, family Begoniaceae: leaf venation palmate, usually; read as {"palmate": "usually"}.

traits.perianth.note: DELTA, Begoniaceae (read 2026-10-16): perianth petaloid, no separate calyx and corolla.

traits.flower_merosity.note: DELTA, Begoniaceae (read 2026-10-16): commonly 2 or 4 tepals (2-5; 10 in Hillebrandia); male flowers two unlike pairs, female often 5. Typical 2 counts one whorl of a male flower.

traits.stamens.note: DELTA, Begoniaceae (read 2026-10-16): stamens many. Typical 30 is my estimate.

traits.life_span.note: DELTA, Begoniaceae (read 2026-10-16): mostly perennial succulent herbs.

traits.leaf_incision.note: DELTA, Begoniaceae (read 2026-10-17): lamina usually uncut, sometimes palmatifid.

traits.flower_symmetry.note: DELTA Begoniaceae (read 2026-10-17): flowers somewhat to very irregular in perianth, stamens or both; c. 920 spp., nearly all Begonia. Regular flowers only in Hillebrandia and some female Begonia flowers.
